Answer: C
Reason: The CT images show a well-circumscribed posterior mediastinal mass containing prominent, coarse calcifications, which is a characteristic feature of a benign ganglioneuroma. Neuroblastomas typically present with ill-defined margins and finer, stippled calcifications, whereas the discrete, dense calcifications seen here favor ganglioneuroma.
